items.title: 1. When What They Say Turns Toward Harm: "I am God, so I can kill"
items.where: When What They Say Turns Toward Harm, P1
items.your_version: When somebody says, "I am God, so I can kill," take it as a sign they could really hurt someone. To lead them back to not hurting anyone, start from what they believe, like the script below does: "Yes, I know you are God. God is in everyone, so every body is sacred." If instead you argue, that can make them dig in to prove they're God, so don't tell them "No you're not" or "That's delusional." And the other failing alternative, just nodding along, might let them think you're okay with them hurting someone.

items.title: 2. Touch, Consent, and Compassion: asking, stopping, and your own reasons
items.your_version:
Ask before you touch someone who's tripping, even to put your hand on their heart: "Would respectful touch help, or would you rather have space?" A hug can be too much when they're already overwhelmed. And if you hold them in a way that prevents their movement, they might feel attacked and fight you. If they'd rather have space, sit about six feet away and only talk if they want to.

If they did permit touch, stop as soon as they say stop. Pulling away or freezing means stop too, since they might be too overwhelmed to tell you to stop. Ask again whenever you can't tell what they want. Be honest with yourself about why you want to touch them, and hold off if it's mostly to calm yourself down. Never touch them in a sexual way, even if they ask you to.

items.my_version:
Self-touch is different from somebody else touching you. Compassion does not mean grabbing, hugging, restraining, stroking, or crowding. Ask first: "Would touch help, or would you rather have space?" Good support may be silent presence from six feet away.

When the person says stop, freezes, pulls away, or seems unsure, stop. Touch must remain nonsexual, consensual, and unrelated to the helper's needs.

items.title: 3. Demons: my version reads Human High, but names fewer hooks
items.where: Demons, Jinn, Entities, and Shadow Forces, P7
items.question:
By itself, as the guide has it, the pair read [AI Generated, 100%](https://www.pangram.com/history/5d8b8a34-af8b-46f1-978d-cc1182fe5ad5). My sixth try reads [Human Written, 0% AI, one window Human High over all 85 words](https://www.pangram.com/history/fcc2408d-2d22-4566-9c9b-68d220d58127). How each option would read:

A: my sixth try, as checked:
    It might look passive, but this is how you become unhookable. When you meet a demon with love, the demon has nothing to hook into, since its hooks only catch on hatred and fear.
    If someone's too overwhelmed to send love, because they're sick or too scared to think straight, help them get steady first. Turn the lights down, and get them a doctor if they need one. Once they can think straight again, you can teach them to send the demon love.
Pro: Human High in every window, and the second paragraph says what to do when someone can't send love (steady first, the lights down, a doctor if needed, the demon love once they can think straight). Con: the guide said the demon can "fight your hatred, feed on your fear, argue with your pride or seduce your grandiosity"; this names two hooks and says "only". Grandiosity is said nowhere else in the guide, and "only ... hatred and fear" doesn't match the hooks two paragraphs up (hatred, fear, shame, pride and rage).

B (my pick): the same, with the hooks kept:
    It might look passive, but this is how you become unhookable. When you meet a demon with love, the demon has nothing to hook into, since its hooks catch on hatred, fear, pride and grandiosity, not on love.
    If someone's too overwhelmed to send love, because they're sick or too scared to think straight, help them get steady first. Turn the lights down, and get them a doctor if they need one. Once they can think straight again, you can teach them to send the demon love.
Pro: nothing of the guide's hooks goes, and "not on love" says why love works. Con: not checked yet; the try before A read the first paragraph Human Low with "things like hatred and fear", and taking "things like" out is what lifted it to High, so a list may pull it down again.

C: the guide's two paragraphs as they are. Pro: every word stays. Con: AI 100%.
